name: Financier - Almond Brown Butter Cakes
headnote: Lan Lam's take on the French mini cake, aimed at a crisp caramelized shell around a tender, moist centre. Browned butter supplies the nutty depth that defines a financier, while almond flour keeps the crumb soft rather than cakey. She calls for flour-based baking spray in the molds so the batter climbs evenly and the tops bake flat instead of doming.

name: Janice Okun's Buffalo chicken wings
headnote: The recipe is Craig Claiborne's transcription of Buffalo News food editor Janice Okun's wings, published in his 1982 book A Feast Made for Laughter. It is the canonical Anchor Bar formula: whole wings split and deep-fried bare - no batter, no breading - so the skin crisps and renders, then tossed in melted butter cut with Frank's Louisiana hot sauce and a splash of vinegar. Celery and a homemade blue-cheese dressing built on scratch mayonnaise are served alongside to cool the heat.

flags: Identity confirmed: ckbk's ingredient head matches the family card exactly (24 chicken wings, about four pounds, deep-fried, with the blue-cheese dressing and homemade-mayonnaise sub-recipes the family card also carries). Note ckbk is paywalled, so the full method and headnote were not retrievable and the headnote above is reconstructed from the confirmed recipe identity rather than quoted commentary. Free full-text runner-ups a human could use instead: https://www.bigoven.com/recipe/janice-okuns-buffalo-chicken-wings/102022 and https://www.astray.com/recipes/?show=Janice+okun's+buffalo+chicken+wings

name: Jell-O Jigglers
headnote: Kraft Heinz's own JIGGLERS formula - the reason it works is the gelatin-to-water ratio. Using only 2 1/2 cups of boiling water for two large boxes, roughly half the liquid of ordinary Jell-O, sets the gelatin firm enough to be cut with cookie cutters and lifted out with fingers. A brief dip of the pan in warm water loosens the slab so the shapes release cleanly.
comment_digest: NO COMMENTS - the Kraft Heinz brand page carries no ratings or reader comments.
flags: Exact match: Kraft's page and the family card both specify 2 packages (8-serving size) gelatin to 2 1/2 cups boiling water, 13x9 pan, warm-water dip to unmold. The family card additionally allows apple juice in place of water, a variation Kraft has published elsewhere.

name: Herbed Cheese and Cracker Bits
rating: 3 reviews shown; no star average displayed
headnote: A Paula Deen recipe, posted to Food.com by user Tearanii, for seasoning boxed cheese crackers into a party snack. Dry ranch dressing mix, dill, garlic powder and celery salt are suspended in oil and shaken through the crackers in a bag, and the long refrigerated rest is what matters - it lets the oil carry the seasoning into the crackers instead of leaving it sitting on the surface. Turning the container occasionally keeps the coating even.
comment_digest: Reviewers mostly report on occasions rather than corrections: the snack is described as addictive and disappears fast at football parties, holidays, movie nights, BBQs and potlucks. One reviewer recognised it from Paula Deen's television show and has made it for years. No one reported a problem with quantities or the resting step.
flags: Same recipe. The family card has two small downward tweaks from the published version - 1/3 cup oil instead of 1/2 cup, and 3/4 tsp celery salt instead of 1 tsp - which read as a deliberate household adjustment rather than a different source. Everything else matches verbatim, including the Ritz Cheese Bits and Hidden Valley Original Ranch brand callouts.
